literal: You all should uphold the former lords' excellent virtue and glorify their great model.
idiomatic: You should carry forward our forebears' virtue and magnify their grand example.

literal: " The former Huaizhou governor Qinglong, former Qinzhou governor Lü Shouen, and others still clung stubbornly to their views; the emperor soothed them all in reply, and they withdrew after being defeated in argument.
idiomatic: " Former governors Qinglong of Huaizhou and Lü Shouen of Qinzhou still held obstinately to the old view; the emperor answered each with reassurance until they were silenced and withdrew.

literal: The emperor was again about to tour the north; Pi was moved to Grand Tutor and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: When the emperor prepared another northern tour, Pi was appointed Grand Tutor and put in charge of the secretariat.

literal: He memorialized repeatedly to decline firmly; an edict cut off further memorials and granted the appointment at his home.
idiomatic: Pi memorialized again and again to refuse; the court forbade further petitions and invested him at his residence.

literal: When the imperial carriage set out from Dai, Pi remained as guardian. The edict said: "The Central Plains are newly founded and need my personal oversight; affairs in Dai are entirely entrusted to the Grand Tutor."
idiomatic: As the emperor left Dai, Pi stayed behind. The edict ran: "The heartland is still being built and requires my attention; everything in Dai is left to the Grand Tutor."

literal: He was given the emperor's own carriage and horses for going to and from the government offices.
idiomatic: He was granted the ruler's own carriage and horses for travel to and from the ministries.

literal: Pi dearly loved the old ways and did not grasp the new style; changing customs and moving the capital to Luoyang, reforming offices and dress, and banning the old speech—all were unwelcome to him.
idiomatic: Pi clung to the northern ways and resisted the new order: sinicizing custom, moving the capital to Luoyang, changing offices and dress, and forbidding the old tongue—all of it displeased him.

literal: Gaozu knew this about him and did not press him, only guiding him with great principle so he would not breed dissent.
idiomatic: Gaozu understood this and did not force him, only setting out the larger rationale so he would not stir opposition.

literal: When court robes were already in use and vermilion dress filled the ranks, Pi still wore ordinary clothes seated at the corner.
idiomatic: Though court robes and scarlet ranks were already in use, Pi still sat in plain dress off to the side.

literal: Only later did he somewhat add cap and belt, but could not polish his bearing.
idiomatic: Only later did he add cap and belt a little, yet he never managed a polished appearance.

literal: Gaozu, because Pi was aged and heavy-bodied, did not strongly demand it.
idiomatic: Gaozu, seeing Pi's age and bulk, did not insist.

literal: When non-Taizu descendants and those of other surnames enfeoffed as kings were demoted, though reduced to dukes they still enjoyed fief revenues—Pi was displeased about this too.
idiomatic: When kings who were not Taizu's descendants or of other surnames were demoted, though cut to ducal rank they still kept fief income—Pi was unhappy even with that.

literal: 〈Doubtful〉
idiomatic: Passage marked doubtful.

literal: The text is deficient.
idiomatic: The text is deficient.

literal: When Gaozu campaigned south, Pi memorialized begging to remain a while longer, planning again for a later effort.
idiomatic: During Gaozu's southern campaign Pi asked leave to stay behind awhile, intending to try again later.

literal: When Minister over the Masses Feng Dan died, an edict ordered the six armies to turn their banners back.
idiomatic: When Minister Feng Dan died, an edict recalled the six armies.

literal: Pi also memorialized because Feng Xi had died at the Dai capital, requesting the imperial carriage attend in person.
idiomatic: Pi also memorialized that Feng Xi had died at Dai and begged the emperor to come in person.

literal: The edict said: "Luoyang is newly founded; eager hope and toil await completion. From the founding until now, how could one with the weight of the Son of Heaven travel far for a funeral in the maternal-kin state?"
idiomatic: The reply said: "Luoyang is only now rising; the realm waits on that labor. Since the founding, when has a Son of Heaven gone far away for a maternal uncle's mourning?"

literal: Even if I wished to act as a filial son, what of the greater filial duty?
idiomatic: Even if I wished private filial piety, what of the greater filial duty to the realm?

literal: Even if I wished to act with righteousness, what of the greater righteousness?
idiomatic: Even if I wished private righteousness, what of the greater righteousness owed the state?

literal: The realm is paramount; the bond between ruler and minister is weighty—how can you lightly entice and lead the sovereign into unworthy conduct?
idiomatic: The empire outweighs all else; ruler and minister stand far apart—how can you coax the throne into discreditable conduct?

literal: The Director and Vice Director and those below may be handed to the judicial officers for demotion.
idiomatic: The Director, Vice Director, and their subordinates are to be referred to the judges for censure.

literal: An edict also appointed Pi commander-in-chief and governor of Bingzhou.
idiomatic: He was also made area commander and given Bingzhou.

literal: Later an edict, because Pingyang lay in the capital district, changed his enfeoffment to Duke of Xinxing.
idiomatic: Later, because Pingyang lay in the metropolitan belt, he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Xinxing.

literal: Earlier Li Chong was one to whom moral standing was attributed; he was then an eminent figure of the time. Pi had a private leaning [15], and his son Chao married Chong's elder brother's daughter—that is, Bo Shang's younger sister.
idiomatic: Li Chong had long stood for integrity and was then among the great men at court. Pi leaned on that tie [15] and had his son Chao marry Chong's niece, the sister of Bo Shang.

literal: Pi's sons by his first wife, Long and several full brothers, all lived apart.
idiomatic: Long and the other sons of Pi's first wife each kept separate households.

literal: Later he obtained palace women; those born to them shared one house and property.
idiomatic: Later palace women bore him children who lived together under one roof and shared the estate.

literal: Father-son affection was thus skewed.
idiomatic: Affection between father and sons was thereby skewed.

literal: Pi and his sons were broadly displeased with the move to Luoyang.
idiomatic: Pi and his sons were deeply unhappy about the transfer to Luoyang.

literal: When Gaozu set out from Pingcheng, Crown Prince Xun remained in the old capital; as he was about to return to Luoyang, Long and Chao secretly plotted to keep Xun behind, raise troops to block the passes, and seize the country north of Xiao.
idiomatic: When Gaozu left Pingcheng, Crown Prince Xun stayed in the old capital; on the return to Luoyang, Long and Chao plotted to detain Xun, cut the passes by force, and hold the region north of Xiao.

literal: Pi was then old and living in Bingzhou; though he had not joined the initial plan, Long and Chao both told him.
idiomatic: Pi was aged and in Bingzhou and had not joined the first design, but Long and Chao both informed him.

literal: Outwardly fearing failure, though his mouth spoke objections, in his heart he rather approved.
idiomatic: Outwardly he doubted success and spoke against it, yet inwardly he inclined to agree.

literal: When Gaozu came to Pingcheng and traced Mu Tai and others as chief plotters, the Long brothers were all accomplices.
idiomatic: When Gaozu reached Pingcheng and fixed on Mu Tai and the rest as ringleaders, the Long brothers were counted among the party.

literal: Pi also followed the imperial progress to Pingcheng; at each interrogation he was made to sit and watch.
idiomatic: Pi followed the court to Pingcheng and was made to sit by while each interrogation proceeded.

literal: Long, Chao, and the Yuan Ye brothers and the rest were all executed for plotting rebellion.
idiomatic: Long, Chao, and the Yuan Ye brothers were all put to death for treason.

literal: The officials memorialized that their families be exterminated to the third degree; an edict held that Pi should share guilt, but because of an earlier promise that he would not die and because he had not personally joined the rebellion, he was spared death and reduced to a commoner of Taiyuan; his later wife and two sons were allowed to follow him.
idiomatic: The court proposed exterminating their kin; an edict held Pi liable yet, citing the earlier pledge of life and his lack of direct guilt, spared him for commoner status in Taiyuan, letting his later wife and two sons accompany him.

literal: Long and Chao's mother-born younger brothers and the remaining lesser brothers were all banished to Dunhuang.
idiomatic: The uterine brothers of Long and Chao and the other collateral kin were exiled to Dunhuang.

literal: Pi was then nearly eighty, yet still loaded his own baggage at Pingcheng and followed the imperial progress to Luoyang.
idiomatic: Though nearly eighty, Pi still carried his own baggage from Pingcheng and followed the court to Luoyang.

literal: Gaozu repeatedly sent attendants to comfort and encourage him; only then did he return to Jinyang.
idiomatic: Gaozu sent attendants again and again to console him before he went back to Jinyang.

literal: When Gaozu died, Pi came from Bingzhou to attend the funeral; Emperor Xuanwu received him.
idiomatic: After Gaozu's death Pi came from Bingzhou to mourn; Xuanwu granted him an audience.

literal: Because Pi was an elder of the former reign, courtesy toward him was increased.
idiomatic: As a survivor of the old court, he was shown added respect.

literal: Soon he was ordered to remain in Luoyang.
idiomatic: He was soon ordered to stay in Luoyang.

literal: Later, at a banquet in the Hualin Pavilion, he was specially allowed two sons to support him in sitting and rising.
idiomatic: Later, at a feast in the Hualin Pavilion, two sons were specially assigned to help him sit and stand.

literal: Pi had served through six reigns for nearly seventy years, reaching the highest ministerial rank yet ending as a commoner; still he yearned for the capital and could not cut himself off from public life.
idiomatic: He had served six reigns for nearly seventy years, risen to chief minister, then fallen to commoner rank, yet still clung to the capital and could not withdraw from the world.

literal: Soon he was appointed one of the Three Elders.
idiomatic: He was soon named one of the Three Elders.

literal: In Jingming year 4 he died, aged eighty-two.
idiomatic: He died in Jingming year 4 at eighty-two.

literal: An edict posthumously appointed him Left Grand Master of Splendid Service and regional inspector of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Ping.
idiomatic: The court posthumously made him Left Grand Master of Splendid Service and inspector of Jizhou, with the posthumous name Ping.

literal: His eldest son Long had earlier been executed for rebellion.
idiomatic: His eldest son Long had already been executed for rebellion.

literal: Long's younger brothers Yisheng and Chao were executed together.
idiomatic: Long's brothers Yisheng and Chao were executed with him.

literal: Chao's younger brothers Jun and Yong both had military merit.
idiomatic: Chao's younger brothers Jun and Yong both won distinction in war.

literal: Jun was enfeoffed Baron of Xin'an; Yong was enfeoffed Baron of Jing.
idiomatic: Jun was made Baron of Xin'an; Yong, Baron of Jing.

literal: Marquis Datou of Huailing was a great-grandson of Emperor Lie.
idiomatic: Datou, Marquis of Huailing, was a great-grandson of Emperor Lie.

literal: Skilled in mounted archery, he was promoted to Inner Third-Rank Gentleman.
idiomatic: Skilled in mounted archery, he rose to Inner Third-Rank Gentleman.

literal: Following Emperor Taiwu he had battle merit and was granted a noble rank.
idiomatic: He followed Taiwu in campaigns, earned merit, and received a noble title.

literal: At the start of Emperor Wencheng's reign he was enfeoffed Huailing.
idiomatic: At Wencheng's accession he was enfeoffed at Huailing.

literal: By nature cautious and reserved, the emperor valued him highly.
idiomatic: Careful and discreet by nature, he was greatly esteemed at court.

literal: He reached General Who Pacifies the North and was moved to Right General.
idiomatic: He rose to General Who Pacifies the North, then Right General.

literal: On his death he was posthumously made Duke of Gaoping, with the posthumous title Lie.
idiomatic: At death he was posthumously made Duke of Gaoping with the posthumous name Lie.

literal: Duke Qi of Hejian was a great-great-grandson of Emperor Lie.
idiomatic: Qi, Duke of Hejian, was a great-great-grandson of Emperor Lie.

literal: In youth he was heroic and imposing; Emperor Taiwu loved his courage and kept him at his side.
idiomatic: As a youth he was towering and bold; Taiwu admired his valor and kept him close.

literal: On the campaign against Helian Chang the emperor's horse stumbled and the enemy pressed the emperor; Qi shielded him with his body, fought the enemy to the death, and the enemy withdrew so the emperor could remount.
idiomatic: In the campaign against Helian Chang the emperor's mount stumbled and the foe closed in; Qi covered him bodily, fought as if to die, drove the enemy back, and the emperor remounted.

literal: That day, but for Qi, the emperor would nearly have reached mortal peril.
idiomatic: That day, without Qi, the emperor would almost have perished.

literal: When the emperor entered the city in plain dress, Qi firmly remonstrated but was not heeded; he then followed the emperor in with several men.
idiomatic: When the emperor entered the city in disguise, Qi protested in vain and followed in with a few men.

literal: Once inside the city was alerted and every gate was shut.
idiomatic: The city soon discovered them and every gate was shut.

literal: The emperor and Qi and the others then entered the palace, obtained a woman's skirt, tied it to a spear, and the emperor climbed it and thus escaped—Qi had strength in this.
idiomatic: They entered the palace, took a woman's skirt, lashed it to a spear, and the emperor climbed out on it—Qi had the strength for that escape.

literal: He was granted the marquisate of Fuyang.
idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Marquis of Fuyang.

literal: On the campaign against Helong he was appointed Master of Writing for merit and advanced to duke.
idiomatic: On the Helong campaign he was made Master of Writing for merit and raised to duke.

literal: Later, with the Prince of Xinxing Jun he attacked Tufa Baozhou and was stripped of office and rank for an offense.
idiomatic: Later, campaigning with Prince Jun of Xinxing against Tufa Baozhou, he lost office and rank for an offense.

literal: When Liu Yilong's general Pei Fangming took Chouchi, the emperor again appointed Qi Forward General and, with Duke of Jianxing Gu Bibie, attacked him; they took Chouchi and awed the Qiang and Di.
idiomatic: When Liu Yilong's general Pei Fangming seized Chouchi, Taiwu again made Qi Forward General; with Gu Bibie, Duke of Jianxing, he recovered Chouchi and overawed the Qiang and Di.

literal: He was again granted the dukedom of Hejian and, with Prince Baozong of Wudu Yang, jointly garrisoned Luogu.
idiomatic: He was again made Duke of Hejian and, with Yang Baozong, Prince of Wudu, jointly held Luogu.

literal: At the time Baozong's younger brother Wende urged Baozong to shut the passes and hold himself fast.
idiomatic: Then Baozong's brother Wende urged him to close the defiles and stand on his own.

literal: The time was set; Qinzhou registrar Bian Yin learned of it and secretly informed Qi.
idiomatic: A date was fixed; Bian Yin, registrar of Qinzhou, learned of it and secretly told Qi.

literal: At dawn Qi went to Baozong and called out: "Gu Bibie has arrived and wishes to proclaim the edict."
idiomatic: At dawn Qi went to Baozong and shouted: "Gu Bibie is here to proclaim the edict."

literal: Baozong came out; Qi ordered his attendants to seize Baozong, put him on a horse, and rush him by post to the capital.
idiomatic: Baozong came out; Qi had his men seize him, mount him, and post him to the capital.

literal: The Di then made Wende their leader and sought aid from Liu Yilong.
idiomatic: The Di thereupon set up Wende and asked Liu Yilong for help.

literal: Yilong sent the generals Fang Liangzhi, Fu Zhao, and Tan Long with troops to aid Wende.
idiomatic: Yilong sent Fang Liangzhi, Fu Zhao, Tan Long, and others to support Wende.

literal: Qi struck, killed Long, and captured Liangzhi.
idiomatic: Qi attacked, killed Tan Long, and captured Fang Liangzhi.

literal: The Di were then pacified.
idiomatic: The Di were pacified.

literal: For merit he was appointed Grand Inner Steward.
idiomatic: For this merit he was made Grand Inner Steward.

literal: On his death his posthumous title was Jing.
idiomatic: At death his posthumous name was Jing.

literal: His eldest son Ling inherited the title.
idiomatic: His eldest son Ling succeeded to the title.

literal: Ling was upright and unyielding; in the first year of Tian'an he was killed by Yihun.
idiomatic: Ling was blunt and unyielding; in Tian'an year 1 Yihun killed him.

literal: Ling's younger brother Lan was favored for loyalty and prudence.
idiomatic: Ling's brother Lan won favor for loyalty and care.

literal: At the start of Gaozu's reign he was granted the viscountcy of Jianyang.
idiomatic: At Gaozu's accession he was made Viscount of Jianyang.

literal: He died as garrison commander of Wuchuan.
idiomatic: He died while commanding Wuchuan garrison.

literal: His son Zhi, courtesy name Menglue.
idiomatic: His son Zhi, styled Menglue.

literal: In youth he was clear in debate and strong in execution; he read widely in books and records and had considerable literary talent.
idiomatic: In youth he was sharp in debate and forceful in action, widely read, and gifted in letters.

literal: As magistrate of Luoyang he did not avoid the powerful; he disputed the road with Censor-in-Chief Li Biao, and both entered audience to state their case face to face.
idiomatic: As Luoyang magistrate he did not yield to the mighty; he quarreled over the road with Censor-in-Chief Li Biao, and both went in to argue their case before the throne.

literal: Biao said: "The censor-in-chief yields to the Chengua carriage canopy, halts for the Way of the sword and drum—how can a Luoyang magistrate contend with a minister?"
idiomatic: Biao said: "The censor-in-chief yields to the Chengua canopy and halts for the imperial sword-and-drum procession—how can a county magistrate stand against a minister?"

literal: Zhi said: "I am magistrate of the divine capital; under heaven who is not a registered household—how can I bow like the common officials and yield to the censor-in-chief?"
idiomatic: Zhi replied: "I govern the sacred capital; who under heaven is not a registered subject—why should I bow like other officials to the censor-in-chief?"

literal: [16] Gaozu said: "Luoyang is my Feng and Pei; naturally we should part ways."
idiomatic: [16] Gaozu said: "Luoyang is my Feng and Pei; of course our roads should diverge."

literal: From now on you may each take a separate road."
idiomatic: "Henceforth you may each keep to your own side of the road."

literal: On leaving, he and Biao measured the road with a folding rule and each took half.
idiomatic: Outside, he and Biao measured the street with a folding rule and each took half.

literal: Gaozu said to Xing Luan: "This boy is truly capable—what they call a lord's son who needs no carving to shine."
idiomatic: Gaozu told Xing Luan: "The lad has spirit—a true prince's son who needs no chasing to gleam."

literal: Luan said: "Frosted branches and dewy twigs have many strong joints; if not a phoenix then a simurgh—they belong on the main bough."
idiomatic: Luan said: "Frosted boughs bear stout joints; phoenix or simurgh, they belong on the parent stem."

literal: Staff member Feng Jun, younger brother of Lady Zhaoyi, relied on his backing to beat the village headmen under him at will.
idiomatic: Feng Jun, an outer-office attendant and brother of Lady Zhaoyi, bullied the village heads in his district at will.

literal: Zhi ordered the chief clerk to arrest and bind him, punished him, and removed him from office.
idiomatic: Zhi had the chief clerk seize him, punished him, and struck him from office.

literal: For this he offended the throne and was demoted to secretary of the Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: This offended the throne and he was demoted to secretary under the Grand Commandant.

literal: Soon he was made Attendant Gentleman.
idiomatic: He was soon made Attendant Gentleman.

literal: On the southern campaign the emperor went in disguise to observe the battlefield; an arrow was about to strike the emperor and Zhi shielded him with his body, so the emperor escaped harm.
idiomatic: On the southern campaign Gaozu went in disguise to watch the fighting; as an arrow was about to strike him, Zhi covered him with his body and the emperor was spared.
